title: Model switch (ml) returns only after the recompute, with its outcome, so one live scene serves a mesh sweep
description:
Tool review 2026-09-20 item 6 (ai-workspace/reports/tool-review-2026-09-20.md). A verify iteration costs a rebuild plus a JVM start per mesh: 137 scene runs (33 min) and 124 builds (63 min) in one session, and a five-mesh sweep in PATCH-115 ran four scenes at 65 to 125 s each. The user's ruling: use the general model load and recompute every ModelScene already has, not a quad-layout route. That path exists: the terminal command `ml <model>` (ModelCommand) resolves the name through ModelCatalog and calls ModelScene.requestModelLoad, and `ixdar-cli terminal "ml bolt"` reaches it. It is unusable for automation because requestModelLoad only sets pendingModelPath and returns; applyPendingModel loads on a later frame and reports success as a bare log line (' loaded <path>') or through reportFailedLoad, so the caller gets 'loading bolt' before anything has run and has no way to learn when the recompute ended or whether it failed. Make the terminal route (or ModelCommand when driven by automation) wait until applyPendingModel has finished and return the outcome: loaded or failed, the exception message on failure, and the load's wall time. Then document the sweep in Ixdar CLAUDE.md (Scenes and visual debugging): `run-scene --keep-alive`, then one `ixdar-cli terminal "ml <mesh>"` plus `ixdar-cli screenshot` per mesh, then `ixdar-cli shutdown`. No per-scene route, no new run-scene flags.

REVISED 2026-09-26 (user ruling): discoverability decides the shape. Nothing an agent reads names the terminal command `ml`: Ixdar CLAUDE.md lists `ixdar-cli terminal` only as "type a line into the scene terminal", and no list of terminal commands is generated anywhere. So the deliverable is an automation route, not a terminal wrapper and not a hand-written CLAUDE.md paragraph. Add a route (suggested path /scene/model, CLI `ixdar-cli model <name>`) whose describe() says what it does, so `ixdar-cli gen-docs` puts it in the generated Automation list of Ixdar CLAUDE.md and in `ixdar-cli --help`. The route resolves the name through the active ModelScene's ModelCatalog exactly as ModelCommand does, goes through the same load path (one code path shared with `ml`, which stays for the user at the terminal), waits for applyPendingModel to finish, and returns loaded or failed with the exception message and the elapsed seconds. `run-scene --keep-alive` prints, in its ready output, that meshes are switched with `ixdar-cli model <name>`, so the hint is in the output an agent reads when it needs it.
definition-of-done:
1. `ixdar-cli model <name>` against a --keep-alive ModelScene returns only after the model has loaded and the scene recomputed; the response says loaded or failed, with the failure message and the elapsed seconds.
2. It is implemented once on ModelScene and works for every ModelScene subclass, with nothing specific to QuadLayoutScene; the terminal command `ml` shares its load path.
3. A load that throws returns failed with the message, and the scene stays alive for the next call.
4. The route's describe() text reaches the generated Automation list in Ixdar CLAUDE.md and ixdar_automation_cli/README.md through `ixdar-cli gen-docs` (no hand-written paragraph), and `ixdar-cli --help` lists `model`.
5. `run-scene --keep-alive` ready output names `ixdar-cli model <name>`.
6. A unit or automation test covers the wait and the failure report.
testing-plan:
1. run-scene --scene quad-layout --keep-alive; `ixdar-cli model bolt`, `model rockerarm`, `model fandisk` in turn, recording each response's outcome and seconds, and screenshot each.
2. `ixdar-cli model does-not-exist` and a model whose load throws both return failed with a message; `model bolt` then still works in the same JVM.
3. Repeat one switch on another ModelScene (cross-field-exam or embedded-tmesh).
4. Run gen-docs and show the new line in CLAUDE.md.
changes-made: Route `POST /scene/model` (`ixdar-app/.../automation/endpoints/scene/SwitchModel.java`, CLI `ixdar-cli model <name>`): resolves the name with `ModelScene.requestModel` (the one resolve+request path `ml`/ModelCommand now also calls), waits on the new `ModelLoadLedger` that `ModelScene.applyPendingModel` finishes with the failure text and wall time, and answers `{ok, outcome: loaded|failed, model, path, seconds, error}`. MeshNodeViewerScene now overrides `loadModelOrGraph` instead of `applyPendingModel` so it goes through the same ledger. RouteDoc gained `positional(...)` params and `waitSeconds`; the CLI turns them into a bare argument and a matching request timeout, and a server command whose answer has `"ok": false` now exits 1. `run-scene --keep-alive` output carries `next` naming `ixdar-cli model <name>`. gen-docs puts the describe() line in CLAUDE.md and README. Tests: `ModelLoadLedgerTest` (4, wait + failure report + timeout + replaced request), 4 new CLI tests; `test_cli` 72 OK.

Verified live. quad-layout --keep-alive (ready output carries `next`: "switch a model scene's mesh with `ixdar-cli model <name>` ..."): `model bolt` loaded 0.73 s, `model rockerarm` loaded 6.25 s, `model fandisk` failed 34.5 s with "java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index -1 out of bounds for size 3" (a real pipeline throw in SnappingCarve.exitBarycentric on master, exit 1); `model does-not-exist` failed "no model matching" plus the available list; a temporary unparseable `*_in_tri.off` (removed afterwards) failed 0.0006 s with "java.lang.NumberFormatException: For input string: \"three\""; `model bolt` then loaded again 0.39 s in the same JVM. cross-field-exam: `model bolt` loaded 0.10 s, `terminal "ml rockerarm"` still answers "loading rockerarm (figure_8)", and the unparseable model fails the same way. embedded-tmesh: `model bolt` loaded 0.31 s. Screenshots under tmp/tool11-*.png. mesh-viewer has an empty model list on this machine, so its switch was not exercised live.
